judgment.reason: The agent understood the Amazon laptop scraping task and produced a JSON list from two Amazon search pages, but it did not satisfy the required workflow of going to each laptop detail page and collecting the requested fields. The final artifact explicitly says fields not visible in search/title text were left blank, and all 42 records have missing requested fields such as Weight, with most missing GPU and Refresh_Rate; agent_steps show only limited detail-page attempts followed by timeouts and a fallback to search-result extraction. The resulting data is therefore partial and not fully evidence-backed for the requested product-page details.

confirmed_observations: Candidate event 46 defines saving after each product. Event 54 calls that save after each loop iteration, including inside bounded batches.

Candidate event 63 reports a 120-second cell timeout and state reset after printing successful rows 25 through 32. Events 66/67 reload exactly 32 records from disk. Saved progress survives worker termination.

Candidate events 70/71 recollect search inventory after recovery: it now contains 42 unique items instead of the original 43 and reports 14 currently unseen IDs. Events 74/75 inspect another page-two result set. The agent did not persist its complete original pending inventory.

Candidate event 82 skips saved ASINs, collects remainingSearch, and saves each result. Event 83 shows rows 33 through 43. Events 86/87 validate and write requested fields, with 43 records labelled observed by the model-written extractor.

The saved final JSON exactly projects the requested fields from 43 canonical saved records. This checks delivery fidelity, not independent factual verification of every field or the extractor's observed label.

Reference has nine tool errors, including two whole-cell timeouts, repeated page/CDP failures, and eventual fallback to parsing search-result titles. It delivers 42 partial records rather than the requested product-page details.
interpretation: Per-record saved output enabled real recovery in the candidate after worker termination. The reference failed amid repeated browser/runtime errors. The pair supports persistence as a useful mechanism, but does not isolate its causal contribution to the score or prove complete source fidelity.
generalized_remaining_problem: Save the pending inventory and extraction code with completed data. Reconstructing a live search after reset changes the task inventory even when saved result rows survive. Current final row count alone cannot prove original cohort coverage.
decision: Keep the frozen runtime unchanged and retain the passing official score. Carry the missing-inventory recovery risk into the full trace synthesis; do not treat a judge pass as proof that recovery preserved all original targets.
